name: MO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +29 partisan lean
Incumbent Wesley Bell running with a large fundraising advantage
Republican challenger has no visible fundraising or outside support
model.rationale: The district's +29 Democratic lean, Bell's incumbency and roughly $3.6 million raised against an underfunded challenger, and markets pricing Bell near 98% all point to a comfortable hold. No polls or expert ratings contradict that picture.
model.watch: A surprise late infusion of outside money for Berry or an unexpected scandal involving Bell could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Wesley Bell, a first-term Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a St. Louis-area district that leans Democratic by about 29 points. He faces Republican Paul Berry and Libertarian Tom Schmitz in November. Bell has raised about $3.6 million and holds over $1 million on hand, with modest outside support on his behalf, while his challenger shows no reported fundraising or outside spending. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race. Prediction markets price Bell's chances near 98 percent. The combination of a heavily Democratic electorate, incumbency, and a large financial edge makes Bell a strong favorite, with the main uncertainty limited to the size of his winning margin rather than the outcome.
